Mango___Anthracnose.symptoms: Dark sunken lesions on leaves, flowers or fruit; fruit may develop black spots and rot.
Mango___Anthracnose.organic_control: Remove infected plant material, prune for airflow, sanitize fallen debris and use appropriate biological/IPM products where locally approved.
Mango___Anthracnose.chemical_control: Use a fungicide currently registered/labeled for mango anthracnose in your jurisdiction; follow the label and pre-harvest interval.
Mango___Anthracnose.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Mango___Powdery_Mildew.symptoms: White powdery growth on panicles, flowers, young leaves or fruit.
Mango___Powdery_Mildew.organic_control: Improve canopy airflow, remove affected material and use permitted biological/IPM options.
Mango___Powdery_Mildew.chemical_control: Use a currently registered mango powdery-mildew fungicide according to the label.
Mango___Powdery_Mildew.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Mango___Bacterial_Canker.symptoms: Dark lesions, cracking and gummy exudation on leaves, twigs or fruit.

Mango___Bacterial_Canker.chemical_control: Use only locally registered bactericidal/copper products for mango bacterial disease and follow the label.
Mango___Bacterial_Canker.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Mango___Sooty_Mold.symptoms: Black superficial coating on leaves and fruit, often associated with honeydew-producing insects.

Rice___Blast.symptoms: Spindle-shaped gray-green to brown lesions on leaves; neck infection can cause panicle breakage.

Rice___Blast.chemical_control: Use a fungicide currently registered for rice blast and follow the label.

Rice___Brown_Spot.symptoms: Brown circular to oval lesions on leaves and grain discoloration.

Rice___Brown_Spot.chemical_control: Use a currently registered rice fungicide when economically justified and follow the label.
Rice___Brown_Spot.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Rice___Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Water-soaked leaf margins turn yellow to straw-colored; leaves may wilt from the tip downward.
Rice___Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.organic_control: Use resistant varieties, clean seed, balanced nitrogen and avoid spreading contaminated plant material.
Rice___Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.chemical_control: Chemical control is limited; use only locally approved products and extension recommendations.
Rice___Bacterial_Leaf_Blight.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Wheat___Leaf_Rust.symptoms: Small orange-brown rust pustules scattered on leaf surfaces.

Wheat___Stem_Rust.symptoms: Reddish-brown elongated pustules on stems and leaf sheaths.

Wheat___Stem_Rust.chemical_control: Use a currently registered wheat rust fungicide according to local extension guidance.
Wheat___Stem_Rust.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Wheat___Stripe_Rust.symptoms: Yellow-orange pustules arranged in stripes on leaves under cool humid conditions.
Wheat___Stripe_Rust.organic_control: Use resistant varieties, balanced nutrition and field monitoring.
Wheat___Stripe_Rust.chemical_control: Use a registered wheat rust fungicide when recommended locally.
Wheat___Stripe_Rust.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Wheat___Powdery_Mildew.symptoms: White powdery colonies on leaves and stems that reduce green leaf area.
Wheat___Powdery_Mildew.organic_control: Use resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen and improve canopy conditions.
Wheat___Powdery_Mildew.chemical_control: Use a registered wheat powdery-mildew fungicide according to label.
Wheat___Powdery_Mildew.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Banana___Black_Sigatoka.symptoms: Dark streaks and expanding necrotic lesions on leaves leading to premature leaf death.
Banana___Black_Sigatoka.organic_control: Remove heavily infected leaves, improve drainage and canopy airflow, and use tolerant cultivars.
Banana___Black_Sigatoka.chemical_control: Use only fungicides registered for banana Sigatoka and follow resistance-management and label instructions.
Banana___Black_Sigatoka.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Banana___Panama_Disease.symptoms: Yellowing, wilting and vascular discoloration; older leaves collapse around the pseudostem.
Banana___Panama_Disease.organic_control: Use clean planting material, resistant/tolerant cultivars, sanitation and strict movement controls.
Banana___Panama_Disease.chemical_control: No reliable curative fungicide for established Fusarium wilt; follow local quarantine and sanitation guidance.
Banana___Panama_Disease.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Banana___Bunchy_Top_Virus.symptoms: Narrow upright leaves, dark green streaking and a rosetted/bunchy appearance.
Banana___Bunchy_Top_Virus.organic_control: Remove infected plants, use virus-free planting material and manage aphid vectors with IPM.
Banana___Bunchy_Top_Virus.chemical_control: No curative treatment for infected plants; vector management should follow local registration.
Banana___Bunchy_Top_Virus.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Cotton___Bacterial_Blight.symptoms: Angular water-soaked leaf spots, vein blackening and sometimes boll lesions.
Cotton___Bacterial_Blight.organic_control: Use resistant seed, certified clean seed, crop sanitation and avoid spreading contaminated material.
Cotton___Bacterial_Blight.chemical_control: Use only locally registered products where recommended; sanitation and resistant varieties are important.
Cotton___Bacterial_Blight.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Cotton___Fusarium_Wilt.symptoms: Yellowing, wilting and vascular browning; affected plants may be stunted.
Cotton___Fusarium_Wilt.organic_control: Use resistant varieties, crop rotation, healthy seed and soil/field sanitation.
Cotton___Fusarium_Wilt.chemical_control: No dependable curative spray exists for established vascular wilt; follow local soil and seed-treatment recommendations.
Cotton___Fusarium_Wilt.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Cotton___Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaf curling, vein thickening and enations; plants may be stunted.
Cotton___Leaf_Curl_Virus.organic_control: Use certified virus-free seed, resistant varieties, remove infected volunteers and manage whitefly vectors with IPM.
Cotton___Leaf_Curl_Virus.chemical_control: No curative treatment for infected plants; use registered vector-control products according to label.
Cotton___Leaf_Curl_Virus.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Papaya___Ring_Spot_Virus.symptoms: Mosaic/mottling, leaf distortion and ring-shaped markings on fruit.
Papaya___Ring_Spot_Virus.organic_control: Remove infected plants early, use healthy seedlings and manage aphid vectors with IPM.
Papaya___Ring_Spot_Virus.chemical_control: No curative chemical treatment exists for infected plants; vector control should use locally registered products.
Papaya___Ring_Spot_Virus.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Papaya___Powdery_Mildew.symptoms: White powdery growth on leaves and petioles with yellowing and reduced vigor.
Papaya___Powdery_Mildew.organic_control: Improve airflow, remove affected leaves and use permitted biological/IPM products.
Papaya___Powdery_Mildew.chemical_control: Use a fungicide registered for papaya powdery mildew according to label.
Papaya___Powdery_Mildew.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Papaya___Anthracnose.symptoms: Sunken dark lesions on ripe or ripening fruit, sometimes with salmon-colored spore masses.
Papaya___Anthracnose.organic_control: Harvest carefully, remove infected fruit, sanitize debris and reduce prolonged fruit wetness.
Papaya___Anthracnose.chemical_control: Use a registered papaya anthracnose fungicide according to label and pre-harvest interval.
Papaya___Anthracnose.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Guava___Wilt.symptoms: Leaf yellowing, wilting, defoliation and decline of branches or whole plants.
Guava___Wilt.organic_control: Use healthy planting material, improve drainage, remove severely affected plants and maintain sanitation.
Guava___Wilt.chemical_control: No dependable curative spray for established vascular wilt; follow local soil/plant-health recommendations.
Guava___Wilt.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Guava___Anthracnose.symptoms: Dark sunken fruit lesions and leaf spots, often worse under humid conditions.
Guava___Anthracnose.organic_control: Remove infected fruit, prune for airflow and reduce prolonged surface wetness.
Guava___Anthracnose.chemical_control: Use a fungicide registered for guava anthracnose according to label.
Guava___Anthracnose.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Guava___Algal_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Orange-red to rust-colored circular patches on leaves, especially in humid conditions.
Guava___Algal_Leaf_Spot.organic_control: Improve airflow, prune dense canopies and remove severely affected leaves.
Guava___Algal_Leaf_Spot.chemical_control: Use a locally registered copper or other suitable product only if recommended for guava.
Guava___Algal_Leaf_Spot.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Onion___Purple_Blotch.symptoms: Small water-soaked lesions enlarge into purple-brown spots with yellow halos.
Onion___Purple_Blotch.organic_control: Use clean seed/sets, adequate spacing, irrigation management and remove infected debris.
Onion___Purple_Blotch.chemical_control: Use a registered onion fungicide according to label and resistance-management guidance.
Onion___Purple_Blotch.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Onion___Downy_Mildew.symptoms: Pale green to yellow patches with gray-violet fungal growth under humid conditions.
Onion___Downy_Mildew.organic_control: Improve air circulation, avoid prolonged leaf wetness and remove infected debris.
Onion___Downy_Mildew.chemical_control: Use a registered onion downy-mildew fungicide according to local guidance.
Onion___Downy_Mildew.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Onion___Stemphylium_Blight.symptoms: Small yellow to brown leaf spots enlarge into dark lesions and can blight foliage.
Onion___Stemphylium_Blight.organic_control: Improve drainage and airflow, use clean planting material and remove infected debris.
Onion___Stemphylium_Blight.chemical_control: Use a registered onion fungicide according to label.
Onion___Stemphylium_Blight.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Cabbage___Black_Rot.symptoms: V-shaped yellow to brown lesions from leaf margins with blackened veins.
Cabbage___Black_Rot.organic_control: Use clean seed, resistant varieties, sanitation and avoid overhead irrigation.
Cabbage___Black_Rot.chemical_control: Chemical control is limited; prioritize clean seed and resistant varieties.
Cabbage___Black_Rot.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Cabbage___Downy_Mildew.symptoms: Yellow angular leaf spots with gray-white growth on leaf undersides.
Cabbage___Downy_Mildew.organic_control: Improve airflow, reduce leaf wetness and remove heavily infected debris.
Cabbage___Downy_Mildew.chemical_control: Use a fungicide registered for brassica downy mildew according to label.
Cabbage___Downy_Mildew.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Cabbage___Club_Root.symptoms: Wilting, yellowing and swollen distorted roots; plants may remain stunted.
Cabbage___Club_Root.organic_control: Use resistant varieties, liming where locally recommended, sanitation and long rotations with non-host crops.
Cabbage___Club_Root.chemical_control: No reliable curative foliar spray; use only locally approved soil treatments where applicable.
Cabbage___Club_Root.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Chilli___Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaf curling, puckering, vein thickening and stunting, often associated with whiteflies.
Chilli___Leaf_Curl_Virus.organic_control: Remove infected plants, use healthy seedlings and manage whiteflies through IPM.
Chilli___Leaf_Curl_Virus.chemical_control: No curative treatment; use registered vector-control products only according to label.
Chilli___Leaf_Curl_Virus.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Chilli___Anthracnose.symptoms: Sunken dark lesions on fruit with concentric rings and possible twig dieback.
Chilli___Anthracnose.organic_control: Remove infected fruit, use clean seed, improve airflow and avoid overhead irrigation.
Chilli___Anthracnose.chemical_control: Use a registered chilli anthracnose fungicide according to label.
Chilli___Anthracnose.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Chilli___Bacterial_Spot.symptoms: Small dark water-soaked leaf spots and raised fruit lesions.
Chilli___Bacterial_Spot.organic_control: Use clean seed, sanitation, crop rotation and avoid working wet plants.
Chilli___Bacterial_Spot.chemical_control: Use only locally registered bactericidal products where recommended; follow label directions.
Chilli___Bacterial_Spot.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Brinjal___Little_Leaf_Disease.symptoms: Very small leaves, shortened internodes, bushy growth and poor fruit development.
Brinjal___Little_Leaf_Disease.organic_control: Remove infected plants and manage the leafhopper vector with IPM and clean nursery practices.
Brinjal___Little_Leaf_Disease.chemical_control: No curative treatment for infected plants; vector management should use registered products only.
Brinjal___Little_Leaf_Disease.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Brinjal___Phomopsis_Blight.symptoms: Circular brown fruit lesions and dark stem lesions that can cause dieback.
Brinjal___Phomopsis_Blight.organic_control: Remove infected fruit, use clean seed, sanitation and avoid prolonged fruit wetness.
Brinjal___Phomopsis_Blight.chemical_control: Use a registered brinjal fungicide according to label.
Brinjal___Phomopsis_Blight.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Brinjal___Verticillium_Wilt.symptoms: Lower-leaf yellowing, one-sided wilt and vascular discoloration.
Brinjal___Verticillium_Wilt.organic_control: Use resistant varieties, rotation, healthy seedlings and sanitation.
Brinjal___Verticillium_Wilt.chemical_control: No dependable curative foliar spray exists; follow local soil-management recommendations.
Brinjal___Verticillium_Wilt.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Groundnut___Tikka_Disease.symptoms: Small brown to dark leaf spots that may cause premature defoliation.
Groundnut___Tikka_Disease.organic_control: Crop rotation, clean seed, residue management and balanced nutrition reduce pressure.
Groundnut___Tikka_Disease.chemical_control: Use a fungicide registered for groundnut leaf spot according to label and local thresholds.
Groundnut___Tikka_Disease.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Groundnut___Rust.symptoms: Orange-brown rust pustules on lower leaf surfaces with yellowing and defoliation.
Groundnut___Rust.organic_control: Use resistant varieties, rotation and field sanitation.
Groundnut___Rust.chemical_control: Use a registered groundnut rust fungicide according to local recommendations.
Groundnut___Rust.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Groundnut___Collar_Rot.symptoms: Brown lesions at the collar with wilting and seedling death.
Groundnut___Collar_Rot.organic_control: Use healthy seed, good drainage, field sanitation and suitable biological seed treatment where approved.
Groundnut___Collar_Rot.chemical_control: Use registered seed-treatment/fungicide options according to the label.
Groundnut___Collar_Rot.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Sunflower___Alternaria_Blight.symptoms: Dark circular to irregular leaf spots that expand and cause blighting.
Sunflower___Alternaria_Blight.organic_control: Use resistant varieties, rotation, clean seed and remove infected residue.
Sunflower___Alternaria_Blight.chemical_control: Use a registered sunflower fungicide according to label.
Sunflower___Alternaria_Blight.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Sunflower___Rust.symptoms: Orange-brown pustules on leaves and sometimes stems.
Sunflower___Rust.organic_control: Use resistant varieties, sanitation and crop rotation.
Sunflower___Rust.chemical_control: Use a registered sunflower rust fungicide when locally recommended.
Sunflower___Rust.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Sunflower___Downy_Mildew.symptoms: Stunting, chlorotic leaves and downy growth on leaf undersides under humid conditions.
Sunflower___Downy_Mildew.organic_control: Use resistant varieties, disease-free seed, drainage and rotation.
Sunflower___Downy_Mildew.chemical_control: Use registered seed/foliar treatment options according to local guidance.
Sunflower___Downy_Mildew.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Tea___Blister_Blight.symptoms: Small translucent lesions develop into raised blisters on young leaves and shoots.
Tea___Blister_Blight.organic_control: Improve canopy airflow, remove severely infected tissue and manage shade/humidity.
Tea___Blister_Blight.chemical_control: Use a tea-registered fungicide according to local plantation guidance and label.
Tea___Blister_Blight.source: Tea Board/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Tea___Red_Rust.symptoms: Orange-red algal patches on leaves and stems, especially on stressed bushes.
Tea___Red_Rust.organic_control: Improve nutrition, canopy management and sanitation; reduce plant stress.
Tea___Red_Rust.chemical_control: Use a registered product only when recommended for tea and follow the label.
Tea___Red_Rust.source: Tea Board/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Tea___Grey_Blight.symptoms: Gray-brown leaf lesions that expand and reduce healthy leaf area.
Tea___Grey_Blight.organic_control: Remove infected leaves, improve airflow and avoid excessive canopy wetness.
Tea___Grey_Blight.chemical_control: Use a registered tea fungicide according to label and resistance-management guidance.
Tea___Grey_Blight.source: Tea Board/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Purple-red to brown spots that enlarge and give leaves a scorched appearance.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.organic_control: Remove infected leaves, improve airflow, avoid overhead irrigation and maintain sanitation.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.chemical_control: Use a fungicide registered for strawberry leaf diseases according to current label.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small dark leaf spots and fruit lesions that may crack or become sunken.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.organic_control: Use tolerant cultivars, sanitation and avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.chemical_control: Use a peach-registered bactericidal program where locally recommended and follow the label.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.source: ICAR/State Agricultural Extension guidance; verify current local label

Banana___Bract_Mosaic_Virus.symptoms: Reddish-brown spindle-shaped streaks on bracts, leaf midribs or petioles; leaves may become distorted.
Banana___Bract_Mosaic_Virus.organic_control: Remove and destroy confirmed infected mats, plant only virus-free suckers or tissue-culture plants, and manage aphid vectors with integrated pest management.
Banana___Bract_Mosaic_Virus.chemical_control: There is no curative pesticide for a virus-infected plant. Use insecticides against vectors only when currently registered for banana and specifically recommended by local extension; follow the label.
Banana___Bract_Mosaic_Virus.source: ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana and State Agricultural Extension; confirm diagnosis and current Indian label

Banana___Healthy.symptoms: No characteristic disease symptoms are apparent in the submitted image; an image scan cannot establish that the whole plant is disease-free.
Banana___Healthy.organic_control: Use clean planting material, balanced nutrition, adequate drainage, field sanitation and routine scouting.
Banana___Healthy.chemical_control: No pesticide is indicated for a healthy plant. Apply a pesticide only after confirming a target pest or disease and checking its current Indian crop label.
Banana___Healthy.source: ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana; integrated crop health guidance

Banana___Insect_Pest.symptoms: Visible feeding injury, holes, scars or damaged leaf tissue; the image class does not identify a particular insect species.
Banana___Insect_Pest.organic_control: Inspect leaf undersides and pseudostems to identify the pest, remove severely damaged material when appropriate, maintain field sanitation, and use physical or biological controls suited to the identified pest.
Banana___Insect_Pest.chemical_control: Do not spray from this broad image label alone. Identify the pest first, then use only an insecticide currently registered in India for that pest on banana and follow the label and pre-harvest interval.
Banana___Insect_Pest.source: ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana; identify the pest before choosing control

Banana___Moko.symptoms: Rapid yellowing and wilting, leaf collapse, vascular discoloration and sometimes bacterial ooze from cut tissues or fruit.
Banana___Moko.organic_control: Treat suspected cases as a serious bacterial wilt: isolate the affected mat, avoid moving soil or tools from the area, disinfect tools, and seek confirmation from a plant-health or agricultural-extension authority before removal.
Banana___Moko.chemical_control: There is no reliable curative spray for an infected plant. Follow official plant-health, sanitation and movement-control directions; do not apply pesticides as a substitute for containment.
Banana___Moko.source: ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana and official plant-health guidance; laboratory confirmation recommended

Banana___Panama.symptoms: Yellowing of older leaves, wilting and collapse around the pseudostem; internal vascular tissues may show reddish-brown discoloration.
Banana___Panama.organic_control: Use clean planting material, resistant or tolerant cultivars, sanitation and strict movement controls; avoid moving contaminated soil, water or tools.
Banana___Panama.chemical_control: There is no reliable curative fungicide for an established infection. Follow local plant-health and quarantine guidance; do not move infected planting material.
Banana___Panama.source: ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana and official plant-health guidance; confirm diagnosis

Banana___Yellow_Sigatoka.symptoms: Pale yellow streaks on leaves that may lengthen and develop brown or gray centers, reducing functional leaf area.
Banana___Yellow_Sigatoka.organic_control: Remove heavily affected leaves when practical, improve drainage and canopy airflow, avoid excessive shade and use tolerant cultivars where available.
Banana___Yellow_Sigatoka.chemical_control: Only use a fungicide currently registered in India for the confirmed banana leaf disease, and follow resistance-management directions and the label.
Banana___Yellow_Sigatoka.source: ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana and State Agricultural Extension; verify current Indian label

Cotton___Diseased_Leaf.symptoms: The classifier detects a diseased cotton leaf but does not distinguish the causal disease; spots, blight, discoloration or distortion may have several causes.
Cotton___Diseased_Leaf.organic_control: Scout the whole field, inspect both leaf surfaces, remove isolated infected residues where practical, avoid prolonged leaf wetness, and confirm the disease before treatment.
Cotton___Diseased_Leaf.chemical_control: This broad class is not a pesticide diagnosis. Confirm the disease and use only a product currently registered in India for cotton and that specific disease, following the label and pre-harvest interval.
Cotton___Diseased_Leaf.source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research; diagnosis-specific Indian label required

Cotton___Diseased_Plant.symptoms: Visible plant stress or disease-like injury; this class does not identify whether the cause is a pathogen, insect, nutrient problem or environment.
Cotton___Diseased_Plant.organic_control: Check roots, stems, leaves, field drainage and recent management; remove confirmed diseased residues and correct cultural stress after diagnosis.
Cotton___Diseased_Plant.chemical_control: No chemical treatment can be selected from this broad label. Diagnose the cause first and use only a currently registered product for cotton and the confirmed target.
Cotton___Diseased_Plant.source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research; diagnosis-specific Indian label required

Cotton___Healthy.symptoms: No characteristic disease symptoms are apparent in the submitted image; this is not a whole-field health certificate.
Cotton___Healthy.organic_control: Use clean seed, crop rotation, balanced nutrition, good drainage and regular pest and disease scouting.
Cotton___Healthy.chemical_control: No pesticide is indicated for a healthy plant. Treat only a confirmed target using a current Indian crop label.
Cotton___Healthy.source: ICAR-Central Institute for Cotton Research; integrated crop health guidance

Guava___Fruit_Fly.symptoms: Fruit may show punctures or soft, discolored patches; larvae feed inside fruit and symptoms can resemble other fruit damage.
Guava___Fruit_Fly.organic_control: Collect and destroy fallen and infested fruit frequently, use orchard sanitation and locally recommended food-bait or trapping methods, and harvest promptly.
Guava___Fruit_Fly.chemical_control: Use bait sprays or other insecticides only when currently registered in India for fruit fly on guava; follow the exact label, pollinator precautions and pre-harvest interval.
Guava___Fruit_Fly.source: ICAR-Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture and State Agricultural Extension; verify current Indian label

Guava___Healthy.symptoms: No characteristic disease symptoms are apparent in the submitted image; this does not rule out latent infection or problems elsewhere on the tree.
Guava___Healthy.organic_control: Use healthy planting material, balanced nutrition, orchard sanitation, good drainage and regular scouting for pests and disease.
Guava___Healthy.chemical_control: No pesticide is indicated for a healthy tree. Treat only a confirmed target with a product currently registered in India for guava and the specific pest or disease.
Guava___Healthy.source: ICAR-Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture; integrated crop health guidance

Papaya___Bacterial_Blight.symptoms: Water-soaked or angular leaf lesions, darkening or blighting of young tissue, and possible wilting; confirm because symptoms overlap other papaya disorders.
Papaya___Bacterial_Blight.organic_control: Use disease-free planting material, remove confirmed infected plants or residues where advised, sanitize tools, avoid overhead irrigation and limit work in wet crops.
Papaya___Bacterial_Blight.chemical_control: There is no general curative spray recommendation from an image diagnosis. Use only bactericides currently registered in India for papaya and the confirmed disease when local extension recommends them; follow the label.
Papaya___Bacterial_Blight.source: ICAR-Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture and State Agricultural Extension; confirm diagnosis

Papaya___Carica_Insect_Hole.symptoms: Holes or feeding injury on leaves; this class identifies visible damage but not the insect or its life stage.
Papaya___Carica_Insect_Hole.organic_control: Inspect the plant to identify the pest, hand-remove pests where practical, remove heavily damaged material and conserve beneficial insects.
Papaya___Carica_Insect_Hole.chemical_control: Do not spray from this broad image label alone. Identify the pest and use only a product currently registered in India for that pest on papaya; follow the label and pre-harvest interval.
Papaya___Carica_Insect_Hole.source: ICAR-Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture; identify the pest before choosing control

Papaya___Healthy.symptoms: No characteristic disease symptoms are apparent in the submitted image; image classification cannot rule out latent or root disease.
Papaya___Healthy.organic_control: Use healthy planting material, well-drained soil, balanced nutrition, sanitation and routine scouting.
Papaya___Healthy.chemical_control: No pesticide is indicated for a healthy plant. Treat only a confirmed pest or disease using a current Indian crop label.
Papaya___Healthy.source: ICAR-Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture; integrated crop health guidance

Papaya___Yellow_Necrotic_Spots_Holes.disease_name: Papaya Yellow Necrotic Spots and Holes (Unspecified)
Papaya___Yellow_Necrotic_Spots_Holes.symptoms: Yellowing, necrotic patches and holes are visible; this combination is nonspecific and may result from disease, insects, nutrient stress or physical injury.
Papaya___Yellow_Necrotic_Spots_Holes.organic_control: Inspect leaf undersides, stems and nearby plants, compare new and old growth, remove confirmed infected debris and seek a crop-specific diagnosis before intervention.
Papaya___Yellow_Necrotic_Spots_Holes.chemical_control: No chemical cure can be selected from this nonspecific label. Identify the cause and use only a product currently registered in India for papaya and the confirmed target.

Rice___Hispa.symptoms: White scraped streaks or blotches on leaves from adult feeding; larvae mine within the leaf and can leave whitish patches.
Rice___Hispa.organic_control: Monitor fields, remove heavily infested leaves in small plots, conserve natural enemies and avoid excessive nitrogen that encourages susceptible growth.
Rice___Hispa.chemical_control: Use an insecticide only if the pest is confirmed and treatment is locally justified; the product must currently be registered in India for rice hispa and be used exactly as labeled.
Rice___Hispa.source: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute and State Agricultural Extension; verify current Indian label

Rice___Leaf_Scald.symptoms: Large lesions begin near leaf tips or margins with alternating light and dark bands and may cause tip drying.
Rice___Leaf_Scald.organic_control: Use clean seed and tolerant varieties where available, manage crop residues and nitrogen, and avoid practices that keep foliage wet for long periods.
Rice___Leaf_Scald.chemical_control: If disease pressure warrants treatment, use only a fungicide currently registered in India for rice leaf scald and follow local extension advice and the label.
Rice___Leaf_Scald.source: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute and State Agricultural Extension; verify current Indian label

Rice___Leaf_Smut.symptoms: Small angular black or dark brown spots on leaves, sometimes with yellow margins; severe infection can cause leaf drying.
Rice___Leaf_Smut.organic_control: Use healthy seed, resistant varieties when available, balanced nitrogen and potassium, and field sanitation.
Rice___Leaf_Smut.chemical_control: Use a fungicide only when the disease is confirmed and locally recommended; verify current Indian registration for rice leaf smut and follow the label.
Rice___Leaf_Smut.source: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute and State Agricultural Extension; verify current Indian label

Rice___Narrow_Brown_Leaf_Spot.symptoms: Narrow brown linear lesions, often between leaf veins, that can coalesce and cause leaf blighting.
Rice___Narrow_Brown_Leaf_Spot.organic_control: Use healthy seed and balanced crop nutrition, manage residues and water appropriately, and choose tolerant varieties where available.
Rice___Narrow_Brown_Leaf_Spot.chemical_control: When economically justified, use only a fungicide currently registered in India for this rice disease and follow the label and local extension guidance.
Rice___Narrow_Brown_Leaf_Spot.source: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute and State Agricultural Extension; verify current Indian label

Rice___Neck_Blast.symptoms: Dark lesions develop at the panicle neck; the neck may girdle and panicles can turn white or break, leaving unfilled grains.
Rice___Neck_Blast.organic_control: Grow resistant varieties, use clean seed, avoid excess nitrogen, plant on time and monitor around panicle emergence.
Rice___Neck_Blast.chemical_control: Chemical timing is crop-stage dependent. Obtain local extension advice and use only a fungicide currently registered in India for rice blast, exactly as labeled.
Rice___Neck_Blast.source: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute and State Agricultural Extension; verify current Indian label

Rice___Healthy.symptoms: No characteristic disease symptoms are apparent in the submitted image; the scan does not assess the whole field or latent infection.
Rice___Healthy.organic_control: Use healthy seed, balanced fertilizer, appropriate water management, sanitation and routine field scouting.
Rice___Healthy.chemical_control: No pesticide is indicated for a healthy plant. Use only a current Indian crop label if a specific pest or disease is confirmed.
Rice___Healthy.source: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute; integrated crop health guidance

Wheat___Healthy.symptoms: No characteristic disease symptoms are apparent in the submitted image; a single image cannot confirm field-wide health.
Wheat___Healthy.organic_control: Use healthy seed and resistant varieties, rotate crops, maintain balanced nutrition and scout regularly.
Wheat___Healthy.chemical_control: No pesticide is indicated for a healthy plant. Treat only a confirmed target using a current Indian crop label.
Wheat___Healthy.source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research; integrated crop health guidance

Wheat___Septoria.symptoms: Elongated tan to brown leaf blotches, often with dark pinhead-like fruiting bodies; lesions can merge and dry leaves.
Wheat___Septoria.organic_control: Grow resistant varieties, rotate crops, manage infected crop residue and avoid dense, excessively nitrogen-rich canopies.
Wheat___Septoria.chemical_control: If disease severity and crop stage justify treatment, use only a fungicide currently registered in India for wheat Septoria and follow local extension advice and the label.
Wheat___Septoria.source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research and State Agricultural Extension; verify current Indian label
